definition: Impassive means showing no emotion; calm and unmoved, especially under stress or provocation.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word impassive. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know impassive should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The bomb-disposal technician stayed impassive as the timer display flickered, her face betraying nothing.
Composed is weaker than impassive: a composed person stays in control but may still show a tight smile or a worried glance, while an impassive one shows nothing at all.
Stony is stronger than impassive — a stony face suggests cold, almost hostile blankness, while impassive simply means unreadable and unmoved.

Expressionless means showing no feeling on the face at a given moment, whatever the cause — boredom, fatigue, or a daydream can all blank a face. Impassive is blankness that means something: staying calm and unmoved under stress or provocation that would crack most faces.

Unmoved reports the inner state: not stirred emotionally by what is happening. Impassive reports the outer one — the face and manner show no emotion, whatever storms inside. A judge may be deeply moved and still look impassive; someone truly unmoved has nothing to hide.
